summary: Issue #573 (deck-builder finding #3, the last item from the architectural review): DeckSurface.Relayout() unconditionally freed and recreated every visible tile on every call, including a plain window resize. Split into Relayout() (full rebuild -- kept for Reset()/Adjust()/the compare overlay closing, since MakeTile/MakeRow bake per-card displayed state -- copy count, compare selection, over-limit color -- into the Control at creation time and never live-bind it, so a persisting card's tile must be rebuilt whenever that state could have changed) and a new Reposition() (reuses tiles keyed by card identity and just repositions them -- safe only for a plain resize, where the card list and every tile's displayed state are unchanged). DeckSurface's own Resized signal and DeckBuilderScreen.Fit()'s window-resize path now call Reposition(); Adjust() and CloseOverlay() still call the full Relayout().
validation: bash tools/check.sh --skip-client passed in full (2277/2277, EXIT=0). Ran the project's own tools/check-deck-builder.sh native probe (DeckBuilderProbe.tscn) end-to-end twice (before and after the required whitespace reformat): DECK BUILDER PASS, zero ERROR/SCRIPT ERROR/Unhandled exception lines in either run, every scripted assertion passed including the exact scenarios this change touches -- quantity adjustment (native quantity edit marks draft dirty, over-limit count gets Core warning -- proves Adjust()'s full-rebuild path still shows live counts, not stale ones), compare selection, and multiple window resizes (small-window/wide-window captures, mat within compact viewport). Visually spot-checked small-window.png, wide-window.png and over-limit.png -- correct layout, correct over-limit red count after a resize and after an Adjust().
